title: Microsoft Teams: open, edit and discuss shared pages inside Teams
summary: Hold: the briefing implies that anyone in a chat can edit a shared page, but Microsoft documents read-only as well as edit access for page sharing. The roadmap details and primary control instructions are supported; minor corrections should complete the workspace control path and acknowledge conflicting Loop documentation and the product-level licensing requirement.

claims.where: controls[0].scope and note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: IsLoopEnabled controls Teams Loop component creation and integration tenant-wide, not per user.
claims.quote: This property controls Loop component creation and integration in Microsoft Teams. It applies to the entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: No admin UI for the Teams IsLoopEnabled switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"IsLoopEnabled" "admin center"'. Read Loop admin configuration and Teams settings reference excerpts; the documented Teams switch is SharePoint PowerShell, while the admin-center Loop checkbox controls workspace creation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether IsLoopEnabled governs opening shared pages inside Teams.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Loop pages Teams opening shared pages admin switch Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy'; '"AllowFluidCollaborate" "Loop" "pages" Teams'. Read Loop admin configuration and messaging-policy reference; none states this opening feature's control.

claims.quote: Navigate to Home > Org settings > Services > Loop. Choose your desired state for Loop workspaces via the checkbox.
claims.fix: Append the documented control to the path: 'Home > Org settings > Services > Loop > Loop workspaces checkbox'. Apply the same completion to the front matter, rendered table and governance checklist.

claims.claim: The Loop creation controls do not restrict access to existing Loop files or workspaces.

claims.quote: Searched: '"Cloud Policy" "Create Loop workspaces" Graph API PowerShell policy configuration'. Read Cloud Policy overview and Loop admin configuration; neither documents an operation that sets this policy.

claims.claim: Loop components are shared as editable even when the organization's default link permission for other files is view-only.
claims.quote: The components are always shared as editable by others, even if your organization is set to create shareable links that have view-only permissions as the default value for other file types.

claims.claim: Editing beside the conversation makes it easier for anyone in a chat or channel to change shared content.
claims.quote: Page and Component Sharing: Grants access to a specific page (not the whole workspace) with options for edit or read-only access.
claims.fix: Replace 'so editing beside the conversation makes it easier for anyone in a chat or channel to change shared content' with 'so editing beside the conversation makes it easier for people with edit access to change shared content'. The component-sharing statement does not establish that every recipient of a shared page has edit permission.

claims.claim: The support article directs users to SharePoint to locate and delete channel page content.
claims.quote: To delete the content: Locate the Loop page in SharePoint. Hover over the item and select More options > Delete, then confirm you want to Delete again.

claims.claim: Existing SharePoint retention settings govern Loop content stored in SharePoint.
claims.quote: When content is stored in SharePoint, the standard SharePoint IT policy is applied.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/loop/loop-storage alongside the sentence about existing SharePoint retention controls.
